title: Time Variation of Fundamental Constants
bottleneck: Quasar absorption spectra have yielded disputed claims that the fine-structure constant varied across cosmic time and space (a spatial dipole). Laboratory atomic clocks bound present-day drift exquisitely, but the astrophysical claims persist at the edge of systematics, and no theory robustly predicts the observed pattern. A confirmed spatial dipole in alpha would violate the Einstein equivalence principle and point to new scalar fields.
why_it_blocks: Confirmed variation would overturn the assumption of immutable laws underlying all of cosmology. A varying constant would also undermine the distance ladder and stellar models that assume fixed microphysics.
current_state: ESPRESSO and ELT-class spectrographs aim for decisive measurements; current results remain contested. The debate hinges on subtle wavelength calibration systematics in high-resolution spectrographs.
